description: The OKF knowledge slot for working souls: consult the soul's accepted OKF bases remotely (no per-instance copy), keep instance knowledge with judgment, and — when the deployment switches harvest on — hand each instance's notes and session to the knowledge harvester through durable custody.

harvest.description: Whether this deployment harvests: on or off (default off). A host fact, set in oats-local.yaml settings.oats.okf.harvest (`oats okf setup --harvest on|off`). A soul may only opt out, with knowledge: { harvest: off }, and that opt-out is absolute. Off means no source registration, no capture and no custody; the harvest-review trigger is independent of it.

harvest-runtime.description: Harness for the knowledge harvester (the oats.okf/knowledge-harvester package soul), independent of the source instance's harness.

harvest-model.description: Optional model pin for the selected harvest runtime, for example to use a cheaper model: a Pi provider/model or a native Claude/Codex model. When omitted, each harness uses its configured default.

bindings-file.description: Absolute host-owned path identifying the version:1 bindings document. Portable binding preparation captures the selected document payload and never rereads this path.

state-dir.description: Absolute host-owned durable state directory for portable bindings. It is never derived from an instance home.

git-timeout.description: Seconds allowed for each Git operation that talks to a remote (clone, fetch, push, ls-remote); default 600. Local object reads keep a short fixed limit. Raise it for large repositories behind slow links.

consult-max-age.description: Seconds a Git base's host-cached accepted commit may age before an `oats okf` consult read refetches the accepted branch; default 300, 0 fetches on every read. `--fresh` always refetches.

inspect.description: Inspect matching live working-memory documents, durable receipts, bindings, the accepted resolution, any legacy local view and scheduler health.

harvest.description: Capture this source into durable custody and request an independent worker.

args.name: native-request
args.description: Captured operations require an explicit absolute backend-only native request JSON; provider owns the worker task.

args.name: worker-mode
args.description: Captured worker mode: prepare or launch (default launch); legacy behavior is unchanged when absent.
